cards.title: World Notes: Father Christmas
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: Father Christmas is an old English name for the spirit of Christmas. Stories say he brings gifts in the middle of winter.
Old English pictures often show him in a long robe with a crown of holly. In America, a figure like him is called Santa Claus.
In Narnia, the Witch made it always winter and never Christmas. So when Father Christmas gets in, it is big news.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. In Chapter 10, the children hear jingling bells. Watch for signs that the long winter is starting to end.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: two word parts that mean together, two jobs for an apostrophe, and endings that change a word.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 10 with your lens. Then answer three questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write a paragraph about one symbol.

notes.wordParts: The word parts com- and con- both mean with or together. combine = to join together. connect = to tie together.
notes.grammar: An apostrophe has two jobs. It joins two words: did + not = didn’t. It shows belonging: Lucy’s bottle is the bottle that belongs to Lucy.
notes.spelling: Some endings change the base word. Double the last letter: run → running. Drop the silent e: hope → hoping. Change y to i: carry → carried.
notes.wgrd: A symbol is a thing in a story that stands for a bigger idea. Father Christmas getting into Narnia is a sign that the Witch's winter is weakening.
vocab: made new again; restored to a fresh state
a person or thing that announces something important is coming

mods.script: [warmly] Here's this week's reading tip. Some things in a story stand for a bigger idea. Watch for things that keep coming back, like the snow, or Aslan's name. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. Lucy's coat wasn't warm enough, but she didn't complain about the cold. Lucy's shows belonging. Wasn't and didn't each join two words. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Think about the question. Tap See what was hiding. Type each whole word.
mods.script: [curious] Look up at the night sky! Constellation. A constellation is a group of stars together in the sky. The front part, con, means with or together. Its twin, com, means the same thing. Read the four words, and tap See what was hiding. Then type each whole word.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Be a word detective with me. Uncombed. Here's the sentence. The children came out of the cave unbrushed and uncombed. One, read the sentence: they just woke up. Two, look for word parts: un, comb, e d. Three, check it. Uncombed means not combed. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap the five words that need an apostrophe.
mods.script: [warmly] An apostrophe has two jobs. Job one: it joins two words. Can, plus not, makes can't. The apostrophe sits where the letters left. Job two: it shows belonging. The dog's bone is the bone that belongs to the dog. Tap Now check your thinking. Then find the five words that need an apostrophe.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Mrs. Beaver tells the children plainly that they cannot reach the Stone Table before the Witch, but they still have a hope.
items.why: She tells the hard truth, and the hopeful part too.

items.t: Father Christmas tells Peter that his presents are tools, not toys.
items.why: He is honest about what the sword and shield are for.

items.t: Lucy says she is not sure, but she thinks she could be brave enough.
items.why: She says how she really feels, even the part she is not sure about.
